summary: Three substantial cuts toward the Phase 5e recovery ceremony, stopping at the substrate boundary before the ceremony state machine itself. Cut 1 (commit 8ea9393) — storage migration to v2 with K_data reuse: new tapit-attest primitives unwrapKData + reencryptRecoverableReuseKData + Wallet.exportRecoverableReuseKData; AnyEncryptedBlob union flows through localStore + walletStore + remoteStore; createWallet writes v2 from day one; unlockWallet dispatches on `v`; saveWallet has three paths (no blob → fresh v2, legacy v1 → upgrade to v2, existing v2 → REUSE K_data — load-bearing for the cascade because rotating K_data per save would silently invalidate every distributed share). Cut 2 (commit 71c9dc6's predecessor, no wait, actually commit between 8ea9393 and 71c9dc6) — recovery-share builders: createShares.ts exports isRecoveryShare, readRecoveryShare, buildRecoveryShareEnvelope (NIP-44 wraps each share to its recipient's pubkey), buildRecoveryShares (splits K_data + builds N envelopes), decryptHeldShare (responder side), holdRecoveryShare (verify+hold+anchor). 2 new round-trip tests covering the full Shamir-encrypted-decrypted-combined loop. Cut 3 (commit 71c9dc6) — DistributeSharesModal launched from CohortEditorModal once a cohort exists; walks N peers with live per-row status (pending → sending → sent / failed) using summarizePublish for uniform language; InboxPanel + HomeScreen routing for incoming recovery-share envelopes (new 'recovery-share-receive' action). D-03 stays loud across all three cuts: only K_data (32-byte symmetric data-encryption key) is ever split; the signing keypair is never touched. All four gates green at every commit.

outcome.notes: [P-001] Storage migration is backwards-compatible: legacy v1 blobs read fine; next save upgrades to v2 transparently. [P-002] K_data reuse across saves is the load-bearing property: shares distributed once stay valid across every subsequent save. [P-003] Numbers stored as strings in recovery-share leaves because leafValue only returns strings — same pattern existing cohort code uses (though that code has a subtle latent bug reading threshold from numeric leaves; flagged below). [P-004] DistributeSharesModal requires the Mycelium transport to be enabled (existing sendEnvelope throws otherwise) — modal handles this gracefully. [P-005] Three new chunks named in bundle-budget. [FEEDBACK→Foreman]: existing createCohort.readCohort has a latent bug — `Number(leafValue(att, 'threshold'))` returns 0 because leafValue only returns strings; threshold leaves are stored as numbers by treeFromObject. The default-fallback of 3 in CohortEditorModal masks the bug. Worth a small follow-on cut to either (a) change CohortEditorModal to store threshold/totalShares as strings (matching what 5e-iii-b-2 does for share envelopes) or (b) add a typed leafNumber helper to tapit-attest. Until fixed, opening the cohort editor after a publish silently resets threshold to 3 from whatever the operator chose.

uncertainty: All three cuts are tested via unit tests but the END-TO-END distribute → receive → hold loop is browser-untested. The DistributeSharesModal sends real envelopes via sendEnvelope which requires the Mycelium transport to be enabled in Settings — the operator's first two-device field test will be the first real evidence the loop holds against actual relays. The ceremony itself (cuts 4-6) is the bigger uncertainty: multi-round protocol-state-machine work that's larger than this whole session.

All prerequisites now landed: library Shamir primitives (5e-ii), v2 backup format (5e-iii-b), Wallet methods (5e-iii-b-2 library half), storage migration (this session Cut 1), share builders + distribute UI + receive routing (this session Cuts 2-3). The recovery ceremony itself involves: new-device first-run detection of cloud-blob-exists-but-no-local-wallet, fresh keypair generation, recovery-request envelope construction, responder modal with strict out-of-band verification gating, share return loop, combine + Wallet.restoreFromKData, recovery-succession credential built via tapit-attest's succession primitive co-signed by M peers. Substantial multi-round state-machine work; one fresh session per operator directive.
